summary: Consistent hashing allows distributed systems to scale servers up or down without shuffling almost all existing keys. Virtual nodes enhance this by evenly distributing traffic across the ring to prevent server hotspots.

key_points.title: The Modulo Trap
key_points.core_idea: Standard `hash(key) % N` routing breaks when servers join or leave, because changing N alters the remainder for almost every key and triggers a massive data migration.
key_points.analogy_or_visual_hook: A musical chairs game where adding one chair forces everyone in the room to scramble to a brand new seat at the exact same time.

key_points.title: The Hash Ring
key_points.core_idea: Consistent hashing maps both servers and data keys onto a fixed circular hash space (0 to 2^32 - 1), where each key routes to the first server it encounters moving clockwise.
key_points.analogy_or_visual_hook: A glowing 12-hour clock face where data packets parachute onto the rim and walk clockwise until they bump into the first server checkpoint.

key_points.title: Painless Scaling
key_points.core_idea: When a node is added or removed on the ring, only the keys sitting in the arc between it and its immediate neighbor need to be reassigned, leaving the rest untouched.
key_points.analogy_or_visual_hook: Slicing a single piece of pizza in half to share with a new friend while the rest of the slices on the tray stay completely undisturbed.

key_points.title: Virtual Nodes (Vnodes)
key_points.core_idea: With few physical servers, random hash placement creates uneven gaps and overloaded hotspots; assigning multiple virtual nodes per physical server scatters labels across the ring for uniform load balancing.
key_points.analogy_or_visual_hook: Instead of three goalies clumped on one side of a circular arena, each goalie spawns ten holographic clones spaced evenly around the entire perimeter.
